statement: Blind annotation from the Beinecke scan alone (canvas '72v (part)' with two wheels; I describe the LEFT-hand wheel, the one with a four-legged animal at the centre; a reduced view of the wheel and a full-resolution crop of the centre). Identification of the panel is an inference, not a reading: f72v2 and f72v3 have the same label groups (18 and 12), so counts cannot separate them. I rely on the fold: on the recto canvas the panels run r1, r2, r3 away from the spine, so on the verso the back of r3 lies furthest left. If that is wrong this annotation belongs to f72v2 and my f72v2 annotation to f72v3. Centre: a clawed quadruped with a raised forepaw, blue dabs and a red spot, a small plant behind it and a short word in another script below. Two rings of nude standing figures without tubs, each with a star and a short label; the 18 outer and 12 inner are taken from the label groups, since the left third of the wheel lies across a fold and stain and I could not count the figures securely. One figure on the right of the inner ring has small red marks at the head. Labels assigned from line ids and unit codes only, words not read; clockwise from the figure at the top by my assumption, so ids may be rotated by a constant within a ring. Ring figures carry generic features only.

features.colour: uncoloured with blue touches and a red spot
features.position: centre
features.note: large quadruped in profile facing left with round ears, a rounded head, tongue or something long hanging from the open mouth, one forepaw raised, clawed feet, a long tail passing down between the hind legs; pale outline with small blue dabs on the body and one solid red spot on the hind leg; a dark word in a different, Latin-like script under the belly; no star in the centre

features.form: small upright spray behind the animal
features.position: centre, above the animal's back
features.note: small tree or plant of a few upright feathery strokes on a thin stem, standing behind the animal
